Priya Shah: Pushed a new compact-history mock for the Versions timeline — trying a 'cluster by day' mode instead of the current dense vertical stack. Thoughts? Eliot Chen: I like clustering. Feels less noisy for teams with many small releases. question: how do we show canary allocations within a cluster? Marta: Suggest inline badges for each cluster (e.g., 5% canary, 1 variant). Hover expands to the mini-traffic graph. Keeps keyboard users from losing context. Priya Shah: Good — mock includes tiny chips. Concern: screen reader announce order when cluster expands. Need to ensure focus lands on the first variant, not the whole cluster header. Samir: Accessibility nit: when expanding, we should use aria-expanded and move focus to the first actionable item. Also announce "Expanded N variants for YYYY-MM-DD". Priya Shah: Agreed. Proposed snippet for the expander: ```html
...
``` Eliot Chen: That looks good. UX question: if a cluster has a live canary, should we show a persistent CTA to pause/resume next to the canary chip? or only inside the expanded view? Marta: Persistent small pause icon makes sense for fast ops, but it needs an accessible label and a confirmation to avoid accidents. Maybe a single-step undo, not a full modal. QA - Nisha: From testing: accidental pauses happen when icons are close. If we keep persistent action, make the clickable area tiny and add a required secondary confirmation via keyboard (e.g., press Enter again to confirm) — preserves speed for mouse, adds friction for keyboard to prevent misfires. Priya Shah: Alternative: persistent action opens a tiny inline confirm row with "Pause canary" + "Cancel" (no modal). That keeps context and is keyboard-friendly. Thoughts on copy? Samir: For the inline confirm, copy should be explicit: "Pause canary — traffic will be routed to fallback immediately." For rollback confirm, avoid forcing typed input; instead require selecting a reason from a dropdown (required) and an additional "Confirm rollback" button. This reduces time-to-recover for incidents. Eliot Chen: UX debate: typed confirmation vs reason selector — typed is safer but slower. For high-frequency rollbacks, typed slows responders. I prefer reason selector + optional notes. Priya Shah: Noted. We'll do reason selector by default, with an advanced option to require typed confirmation for orgs that opt into stricter safety. design-bot: New mock uploaded: https://redwood.design/mocks/versions/clustered-v2 — comments enabled. deploy-bot: Canary traffic example: 7% -> 30% -> rollback triggered. Logged as 1925012345-rollback-example in test workspace. Marta: One more accessibility thing — when a rollback happens, the timeline should announce a live toast with focusable "View details" link. Screen reader should read "Rollback completed for version 2026-06-12, reason: performance regression." QA - Nisha: Test checklist I can run: 1) keyboard expand/collapse clusters 2) screen reader order when expanded 3) pause inline confirm keyboard flow 4) rollback flow with reason selector + announcement. Will post results by EOD. Priya Shah: Thanks — I'll update the mock to include inline confirm and aria attributes, and add the reason dropdown in the rollback modal. Back soon with iteration. :thumbsup:
